text:
Maya (Support): FYI Acadia reported 429s on /v1/rerank at ~2026-03-16T18:42 PDT. They say only rerank traffic is failing; generate/embeddings are fine. Customer sent a short log snippet and a sample payload.

Diego (SRE): Can you paste the exact response headers/body they saw? Any x-rate-limit headers or retry-after?

Maya (Support): Paste from customer (redacted):

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-limit-limit: 600
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 15
retry-after: 15
Content-Type: application/json
{"error":"rate_limited","message":"Rate limit exceeded on rerank"}

Maya (Support): They said this only started after a large batch rollout on their side; they sent a bunch of rerank calls with ~200 candidates each and then client retries.

Priya (Eng-ML): Rerank cost is higher-per-call since we score many candidates. We usually have a separate quota, but last week's routing change accidentally consolidated rerank + generate into a shared bucket for some orgs. Could be a "false positive" where rerank bursts exhaust a bucket intended for mixed traffic.

Diego (SRE): Confirming what Priya said — saw an internal trace for org_acadia at 2026-03-16T18:42:
```
internal: policy_eval route=\/v1\/rerank org=org_acadia bucket=shared_topline limit=600/min tokens_left=0 drop=true reason=burst_size(420>300) trace_id=tr_0f2a
```

Diego (SRE): So the limiter dropped requests because the token bucket was drained by a short burst of heavy rerank calls. Looks like the bucket is per-org-per-plan but shared across multiple routes; that was the recent deploy change.

Maya (Support): Customer also sent their request sample for repro: (redacted)
curl -X POST https:\/\/api.redwood.ai\/v1\/rerank -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"query": "best hotels", "candidates": [ ... 200+ items ... ] }'

Priya (Eng-ML): Two things: (1) Recommend we document a practical candidate limit (e.g., 100) to avoid these surface bursts, and (2) long-term we should split rerank into its own rate bucket or weight tokens by cost-per-call.

Diego (SRE): Immediate mitigation options: temporarily increase org quota for org_acadia (minutely), add a short-lived exemption for /v1/rerank for 1 hour, or throttle rerank separately at edge with a slower refill to smooth bursts. Which do we want to do while we patch? @oncall please advise.

Maya (Support): Customer is asking for a fast remediation — they hit a live outage for users. I'll ask for permission to apply a temporary quota bump.

Diego (SRE): I'll prepare a 2x per-minute bump and open a runbook ticket. Also adding a monitoring alert to track "drop=true" events on route=\/v1\/rerank.

ops-bot: Quota change: org=org_acadia action=quota_bump delta=+2x scope=minutely expires=2026-03-16T20:00:00Z by=diego_sre

Maya (Support): Told customer we've applied a temporary bump and are investigating root cause. They've confirmed diminished 429s but will monitor for a couple of hours.

Priya (Eng-ML): Follow-ups: 1) Roll back the change that consolidated buckets or roll forward a patch that splits rerank into its own queue; 2) Add docs + SDK guidance on client-side backoff and candidate limits; 3) Consider cost-weighted token accounting for heavy routes.

Diego (SRE): I'll own the rollout/patch and telemetry. Maya — please keep the ticket open and collect exact timestamps+sample request ids from the customer for tracing.

Maya (Support): Will do. Leaving thread open until postmortem note and customer writeup are posted. :thumbsup:
